survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2024 note reports results based on self-reported survey responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals in Bulgaria. The note does not describe the underlying TALIS sampling design details (e.g., stratification/clustering) or specify whether complex survey weights were applied in the production of the reported percentages and statistically significant differences. Because this is a descriptive results note rather than an analysis paper, the manuscript does not provide weight variable names or replicate-weight procedures. Users should rely on the OECD TALIS 2024 Database documentation for the official weighting and variance estimation approach used to generate the reported estimates and OECD-average comparisons.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive TALIS results note based on teachers’ and principals’ self-reports (percentages and agreement rates), not an achievement assessment with plausible values. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the reported outcomes. The note also does not report a specific missing-data handling strategy for non-response or item non-response, so missing-data handling is marked as not_reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note states that it presents findings based on responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals in Bulgaria. It does not provide the analytic sample size or describe additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., response-rate thresholds, item non-response rules), beyond noting that only statistically significant differences or changes are commented on.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024: Bulgaria note summarizes descriptive indicators from the TALIS 2024 survey, focusing on lower secondary teachers and principals. It reports teachers’ background characteristics (age distribution, gender, non-teaching work experience), perceptions and practices related to teaching for today’s world (e.g., adapting teaching to cultural diversity), and school context indicators (e.g., shares of students with non-native first language, refugees, and special education needs). It also covers teachers’ social and emotional learning competencies and confidence, technology use (including AI use in the prior 12 months), and teachers’ learning opportunities (initial teacher education, induction/mentoring, and continuous professional learning). Results are presented as percentages and are compared to an OECD average; the note explicitly comments only on statistically significant differences or changes and cautions that some estimates may be affected by non-response bias. No student-level achievement modeling, plausible values, or ML prediction is conducted in this note.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The document is a country results note rather than an empirical ML study: it does not report an analytic sample size, model specifications, or predictive performance metrics. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, plausible values, and missing-data handling are either not applicable or not reported, and no structured predictive findings can be extracted.
